events.title: Constantine defeats Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge
events.description: Constantine's army defeated his rival Maxentius outside Rome, and Maxentius drowned in the Tiber. Constantine credited the Christian God with his victory and went on to legalise and favour Christianity.
events.html: Constantine's army defeated his rival Maxentius outside Rome, and Maxentius drowned in the Tiber. Constantine credited the Christian God with his victory and went on to legalise and favour Christianity.

events.title: The Byzantine Empire recovers Antioch from Arab rule
events.description: Byzantine commanders ended a siege begun in November 968 and took the strategically important city of Antioch from the Hamdanid dynasty, recovering it from Arab rule.
events.html: Byzantine commanders ended a siege begun in November 968 and took the strategically important city of Antioch from the Hamdanid dynasty, recovering it from Arab rule.

events.title: Beijing becomes the official capital of the Ming dynasty
events.description: Beijing was officially designated capital of the Ming dynasty in the year the Forbidden City, the new imperial residence built from 1406, was completed. It became the empire's primary capital, with Nanjing as co-capital.
events.html: Beijing was officially designated capital of the Ming dynasty in the year the Forbidden City, the new imperial residence built from 1406, was completed. It became the empire's primary capital, with Nanjing as co-capital.

events.title: Christian I is crowned king of Denmark
events.description: Christian I, elected king of Denmark in 1448 and the first king of the House of Oldenburg, was crowned in Copenhagen Cathedral. He later became king of Norway and, briefly, Sweden, and founded the University of Copenhagen in 1479.

events.title: Ladislaus the Posthumous is crowned king of Bohemia
events.description: Ladislaus the Posthumous, son of Albert II of Germany, was crowned king of Bohemia. George of Poděbrady, who governed Bohemia as his regent, remained in control of the government and was elected king in 1458.
events.html: Ladislaus the Posthumous, son of Albert II of Germany, was crowned king of Bohemia. George of Poděbrady, who governed Bohemia as his regent, remained in control of the government and was elected king in 1458.

events.title: Columbus reaches Cuba
events.description: On his first voyage, Christopher Columbus landed on the north-east coast of Cuba. Convinced he was near Asia, he sent envoys inland in search of the court of the Great Khan.
events.html: On his first voyage, Christopher Columbus landed on the north-east coast of Cuba. Convinced he was near Asia, he sent envoys inland in search of the court of the Great Khan.

events.title: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated in New York Harbor
events.description: President Grover Cleveland dedicated Liberty Enlightening the World, a gift from the people of France, on Bedloe's Island. The statue became a symbol of welcome for millions of immigrants.
events.html: President Grover Cleveland dedicated Liberty Enlightening the World, a gift from the people of France, on Bedloe's Island. The statue became a symbol of welcome for millions of immigrants.

events.title: Italy invades Greece from Albania
events.description: Mussolini's forces invaded Greece after Prime Minister Metaxas rejected an ultimatum. The Greeks drove the Italians back into Albania, and Germany invaded the following spring to rescue its ally.

events.title: Angelo Roncalli is elected Pope John XXIII
events.description: The 76-year-old patriarch of Venice was elected pope, widely seen as a caretaker. Within three months he announced the Second Vatican Council, which transformed the Catholic Church.
